content.tldr: Chunking strategies balance semantic coherence against retrieval granularity, transitioning from fixed-size sliding windows to document-aware semantic and recursive markdown splitting.
content.simple_explanation: Chunk size governs the trade-off between retrieval recall and precision. Small chunks (128-256 tokens) yield precise vector embeddings but lose surrounding conversational context. Large chunks (1024+ tokens) capture complete topics but dilute specific semantic signals with noise. Production architectures employ recursive character splitting respecting markdown headers, semantic similarity breakpoint splitting, or parent-document retrieval where small chunks are matched but full parent sections are injected.
content.real_world_example: Indexing an encyclopedia: fixed chunking might arbitrarily slice a person's biography in half mid-sentence, while structural chunking keeps each section heading, paragraph, and table as an intact unit.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: Fixed-token splitting without chunk overlap routinely breaks critical sentences in half, causing vector similarity to fail entirely on the split concepts. Always maintain a 10-20% sliding window overlap.
